terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A parked vehicle prop: an exterior shell with no interior geometry, since a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside and the glazing is authored as a tinted, mostly opaque pane. The wheels are the mechanisms: each is a named pivot on its axle. Nothing else moves and nothing attaches, so there are no sockets. The best-selling vehicle in Thailand: a working double-cab pickup. The plate shows a muted blue extended cab with a quarter light behind the door, a chrome-barred grille between clear rectangular lamps over a black bumper, black wheel-arch flares, chunky mud-terrain tyres on dished steel wheels, a solid tan mud wash over the sills and lower doors with spray behind both wheels, black window gaskets, and a short open bed with a ribbed liner and black rail caps.

reasoning: The identity is the side profile -- bonnet, raked screen, cab, open bed -- and it is one closed polygon swept across the width, with the wheel arches cut into it as notches, then narrowed above the belt for tumblehome. One geometry carries the whole shell.
One repetition system: four wheels off one lathe, each a named pivot on its axle.

Three materials, because a colour difference is not a material difference: the paint carries the mud envelope with the clean blue on a canvas tile, and every trim tone -- tyre, rim, bumper, lamp, liner -- is a vertex colour on one white material.
Action readiness is the wheels: four hinge pivots, convex collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A pickup cannot be a box on a box: the raked screen, the tumblehome and the arches are what make it read as a truck at prop distance, and all three come from shaping one extrusion. The bed is open, so its walls, bulkhead and tailgate are boxes merged into the same shell, and the glasshouse is a second extrusion of the cab polygon offset 6 mm proud so no pane shares a plane with the body.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The plate shows an EXTENDED cab (one long door and a quarter light a side); the registry text says double-cab. The plate is the authority for the build, and the rear handle is placed on the quarter panel as the rear-hinged access door of an extended cab.
The rear elevation is built to type: a flat tailgate with a recessed skin, vertical tail lamps and a black bumper. Not visible in the plate.
Mirrors reach 1.03 m either side of centre; the registry width of 1.86 is the body width.
No interior. The cab is a solid in paint under a 6 mm proud tinted pane at opacity 0.92, so the glass reads as glass and not as a hole through the wall.

THIRD PASS (2026-09-01), feature by feature against the plate: mud-terrain tyres under 0.10 m black flares, a solid tan mud wash zoned behind the wheels, black window gaskets and B-pillar, a chrome-surrounded five-bar grille with an air dam and indicators, body-colour mirror heads, black rail caps, a ribbed liner floor and a pressed tailgate.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 1.86 x 1.82 x 5.33 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=8000 triangles, <=6 draw calls, <=4 materials, <=8 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus one named pivot per wheel (4); zero sockets; convex collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center at tyre contact, +Y up, +Z FORWARD, +X the vehicle's left. Meshy returned the proxy with its long axis on X, an arbitrary output convention; the band comparison detects the mismatch from the two footprints and rotates the reference a quarter turn before measuring.

silhouette.description: Sill at 0.42 m, wheels 0.75 m in diameter (0.80 over the tread lugs) and 0.30 m wide on an 0.80 m track at z +1.715 and -1.37 (3.085 wheelbase, 0.95 front overhang), bonnet lip at 0.86-0.94 m rising to a scuttle at 1.08 m, windscreen raked from z 1.45 to a roof at 1.80 m over 0.12 m corner arcs, a vertical cab back at z -0.72 dropping to a bed floor at 0.80 m, bed rails at 1.20 m to a tailgate at z -2.60. Roof width 0.83 of the body. The silhouette events are the nose, the raked screen, the cab step down to the bed and the two arches. Sheet metal crowns over a 0.13 m shoulder fillet from the cab back to the top of the rake and wraps a 0.24 m plan radius at the nose (0.06 at the tail).
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -0.93..+0.93 on the body shell (the door mirrors reach +-1.03 and are reported, as a real Hilux is 1.855 m over the body and ~2.1 over its mirrors); y 0.00 (tyre contact) to 1.80 (roof); z -2.665..+2.665 bumper to bumper, +Z forward. The registry declares the real vehicle; the Meshy proxy normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.437 : 0.448, a truck only 2.29 lengths tall, so heights were read off the proxy as fractions of H and stations as fractions of L, and the declared metres win on both axes.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.437 : 0.448 -- a truck 2.29 lengths tall against the real 2.93. The area-weighted band table (scratch/_mon/bands.mjs) therefore reads a mean |delta depth| of 0.44 of height that is almost entirely that declared aspect: at bands 2-5 the proxy's depth is 2.04-2.16 H and the candidate's 2.76-2.86 H, and 5.33 / 1.82 = 2.93. The proxy's heights agree with the plate (roof 1.00 H, belt and bed rail 0.66 H, wheel top 0.40 H, sill 0.26 H) and are what was built. Its cab width at the top three bands (0.72-0.80 H) is narrower than the first build's 0.94, which is why the tumblehome was deepened to 0.17.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.75: the plate shows the front three-quarter and the bed from above; the tailgate face, its lamps and the rear bumper are built to the type (a plain tailgate with vertical lamps either side) and to the proxy's rear elevation.

localOverrides.region: sills, lower doors, bed sides and arches
localOverrides.evidence: Sill crop #887d71 against the roof's #3a5176. Delivered on a 512 px tile spanning the 5.33 m length (u) by 2 m of height (v): a solid wash to 0.30 of the tile (0.60 m) fading out by 0.40, 240 spray streaks and 4000 speckles concentrated in zones behind the front wheel (u 0.04..0.24, weight 4), behind the rear wheel (0.51..0.68, 3) and ahead of the rear arch (0.81..0.87, 1.5), a 0.08 dust film everywhere, and upward faces keyed into the clean band so the bonnet and roof stay clean at any height.

evidence: Clean paint measured on viewEvidence region-paint (roof #3a5176, bonnet #34537a, PBR confidence 0.751), authored #36507a; the dried mud on the sill (region-sill, 520..580 x 690..720) measures #887d71, a TAN brighter than the paint in red and green and darker in blue, so the material carries E = the per-channel MAX of the two (#968776) and the canvas paints the clean blue as ratio(clean, E) and the mud as ratio(mud, E), both formed in linear space, so neither is clamped.

The mud is authored #968772 (luma 137) against the crop's 126: the wash sits on the flank the key light never reaches, rendering at ~0.56 of the authored value, and a 50/50 blend of tan over blue is a neutral within 24 RGB of the harness grey that the turntable gate classes as backdrop; the wash is therefore solid to 0.60 m with a 0.20 m edge rather than a metre-long fade.
Textureless as DECLARED: the mud is a seamless 512 px Canvas 2D tile bound after material construction as map, so no procedural texture set is synthesised. Body vertex colours are white.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Three components and one repetition system: 4 of 6. The bed and the pillars ride the shell; sixty-two trim parts ride one merge; the tread lugs ride the wheel lathe.

materials.note: paint, glass and a white vertex-coloured trim: 3 of 4. Tyres, rims, bumpers, lamps and the liner differ in albedo only.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 7,402 of 8,000: one extrusion with two 8-segment arches over 14 width columns, six pillar strips, a 24-segment steel-wheel lathe with twenty lug boxes, and boxes.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A closed side-profile polygon extruded across the width in 14 edge-biased columns and shaped per vertex (tumblehome above the belt, plan taper, a shoulder fillet along the roof edge, plan-radius nose and tail, angle-limited smooth normals); an offset extrusion of the cab polygon for the glass; a lathe for the wheel; boxes for everything else.
One InstancedMesh carries the four wheels; the right-side instances are yawed a half turn so the dish faces out. No per-instance colour, so the white base is inert.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. ONE 512 px Canvas 2D mud tile is bound after construction as the paint map: base is the clean-paint ratio of the per-channel-max envelope, mud is its own ratio as a solid wash, zoned streaks and speckle, and a dust film, all formed in linear space. 1.3 MB of texture VRAM.

risks.description: The proxy is 2.29 lengths tall; the real truck is 2.93. The band table's depth residual is that ratio.
